_comment: Hand-curated recovery policy, one entry per URL. Nothing in this file is
written by the tool, and no fetched page can add to it: a source that asks
to be read from somewhere else is content, not configuration.
canonical_sources: a publisher's current index/sitemap the resolver may
search before asking an archive. A migration by the author is not a mirror.
author_copies: material supplied by the author. Import records provenance
and a hash; the local path is never stored or published.
mirror_sources: an independent republication, used only after canonical.
urls: per-URL pins. 'depth' pins one reference lighter than the repository
default; 'snapshot' pins one exact capture; 'canonical' pins the current
location for a page whose migration the maintainer verified.
decisions: per-URL judgement about whether the archive keeps a document at
all. Keyed by URL. {outcome: archive|skip, class, reason}. A rule never
overwrites one of these, and a skip is not fetched again: the reason is
what the next run reads instead. Use it for the two things no rule can
safely decide - a page that restates a source already archived, and a
tool's usage page with no technique in it.

canonical_sources.reason: Author-confirmed migration: every cited item moved under the current blog collection, including some PDFs. Search here before Wayback.
